# Video Demonstrations to Robot Actions

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](video-to-robot_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Models → Demonstration Acquisition and Action Conversion → Video Demonstrations to Robot Actions

Recover manipulation from real or generated videos and convert it into executable dexterous robot actions. Record scene assumptions and physical refinement; distinguish trajectory replay from closed-loop policy deployment. Retargeting and RL are method tags, not automatic inclusion criteria.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.DEMO.V2R.2] <a id="am-man-dex-demo-v2r-2"></a> | [DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.35318v2)<br>Youhui Wang et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `video-to-robot` `human2sim2robot` `agentic-data-generation` `simulation-verification` `trajectory-optimization` `tool-library` `data-augmentation` `vla-fine-tuning` `sim-to-real` `bimanual` | **Human2Sim2Robot:** One human demonstration video + task instruction → decompose subtasks and identify object properties → reconstruct a simulation scene → obtain a successful robot trajectory through optimization or code generation with simulation verification → vary initial object/robot states to augment demonstrations and process rendered appearance → fine-tune π₀.₅ on the generated data → deploy on real dexterous hands.<br>**Distinction:** An agent selects or writes tools at each stage and revises outputs using verifier failure feedback. New tools and verifiers persist for later videos; self-evolution means accumulating reusable code, with verification acting during data generation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Bimanual YamBox with two Sharpa hands; 11 tasks. Each task uses one human video and 500 augmented robot demonstrations to fine-tune π₀.₅, evaluated over 10 closed-loop trials with randomized initial object states: 63.6% mean success versus 18.2% for SPIDER, the strongest baseline. Separate open-loop replay passes 11/11 tasks, meaning at least one success in ten trials per task, not perfect trial success. Tasks include rigid, articulated, rope and long-horizon interactions; simulation checks do not eliminate sim-to-real or force-sensitive failures. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.35318v2) · [Project](https://dexagent1.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-23 |
